summary: Backend-only retest of the quota-detection fix for AI prospecting. 45/45 tests pass: 18 new unit/method tests in test_prospecting_quota_markers.py plus 27 regression tests (ai_credits, requeue, watchdog) run live against the preview LLM key, which returns real Gemini 429 errors. Results: (1) _QUOTA_MARKERS/QUOTA_REGEX match the Gemini 429 'exceeded your current quota', RateLimitError, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, 'No deployments available', 'overloaded' and the old 'spend limit' errors. They do not match timeout, bad JSON or connection errors. (2) _ask: a quota error on PRO retries once on FLASH. If FLASH also fails, AiCreditsOut is raised and ai_blocked_at/ai_blocked_reason are set. FLASH does not retry itself, and a non-quota PRO error does not fall back. (3) An enrich() hit by a 429 goes back to discovered with enrich_attempts unchanged. (4) requeue_failed returns 429 and 'No deployments' failures to discovered at once, with no retry_rounds increase, even when the brand is at max rounds. Quota contact failures are also cleared. (5) A live /api/prospecting/run stopped in about 17-20s with ai_blocked_reason holding the real 429 text. 0 new failed brands and 0 stuck in enriching. (6) Watchdog writes watchdog_action='ok' when prospecting is disabled and 'restarted' when it is enabled. Final state: prospecting enabled=false, all TEST_ prospects removed, 0 failed brands in the preview DB.

minor.issue: The marker '429' is a plain substring check, and 'budget' is a broad word. Any error text containing '429' (for example inside an id or a number) is treated as a quota error and stops all lanes. Low risk, but a word-boundary regex like '\b429\b' would be safer.

'overloaded' (a short 503-type error) is now treated as quota, so one overloaded reply stops the whole 14-minute batch. Nothing runs again until the next cron or hourly watchdog. That fits the 'retrying' pill, but it is an unnecessary loss of throughput. Consider a short backoff and retry for overloaded before raising AiCreditsOut.

minor.endpoint: core/prospector.py run_worker finally (carried over from iteration 9)
minor.issue: When a stuck run finally exits, its finally block still sets until='' and can release the lock of a newer, watchdog-started batch. Not addressed in this round.

action_items: Optional: use a word-boundary match for '429' in quota detection.
Optional: retry briefly with backoff on 'overloaded' before stopping the batch.
Optional (from iteration 9): use a run token so an old run's finally block cannot clear a newer run's lock.
critical_code_review_comments: Quota detection still relies on matching error text. Checking the exception class too (litellm RateLimitError, or a status_code attribute of 429) would hold up if the provider changes its wording again.
When the AI is blocked, there is no auto-retry inside a batch. Recovery depends on the cron/watchdog schedule, so make sure the production cron interval matches the 'retrying' message.
